content.text:
**Here are the 5 most notable recent tweets** (from the last 48 hours, i.e., since Aug 9, 2026) discussing AI code review, AI judges for PRs/bounties, and human PR review as the bottleneck in fast-moving AI-agent projects:

- **@saltyAom** (309 likes): Argues that mass low-quality AI PR submissions are far more exhausting to review than subpar human code. Reviewers now spend much longer figuring out if an AI-generated PR has any real purpose (“karma farming”) versus quickly rejecting obvious human slop.[[1]](https://x.com/saltyAom/status/2086873369635611106)

- **@gippp69** (102 likes): Highlights PR-Agent (12k+ stars), an open-source AI code review loop that analyzes diffs, summarizes changes, finds issues, and suggests fixes for every PR. Warns against letting coding agents blindly approve their own 1,000-line PRs.[[2]](https://x.com/gippp69/status/2086423052082901302)

- **@nykdotdev** (67 likes): Notes that agents have removed the coding bottleneck, but senior domain judgment remains the scarce resource. One PE operating partner described the challenge of staffing for autonomy and judgment in AI-driven teams.[[3]](https://x.com/nykdotdev/status/2086408661073871019)

- **@heydathan** (4 likes): Identifies PR review as the biggest bottleneck and shares an experiment: using an agent to mine past PR comments, extract deterministic rules into CI/linters, and build a code-review sub-agent + readability doc for the non-deterministic parts.[[4]](https://x.com/heydathan/status/2086895685069422708)

- **@anayatkhan09** (0 likes, but highly relevant reply): Points out that even if individual AI PRs are high-quality, an “agent farm” submitting hundreds of PRs per day overwhelms human maintainers’ review capacity — it’s fundamentally a throughput problem.[[5]](https://x.com/anayatkhan09/status/2086801430732738708)

These posts directly capture the tension between AI-generated volume and human review limits in agentic coding workflows.
